clusters.title: [Impact] KB5060001 on Config1 - Win32k may change WPF windowing or DPI
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:win32k-wpf:Config1 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Kernel Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5060001](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-12345) | CVE-2026-12345 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: Config1
- Model / role: CTConsole-A300 / ct-imaging-workstation
- Deployment group: imaging-ct
- OS: Windows 11 IoT Enterprise build 10.0.22621.2500
- Clinical criticality: high
- Network exposure: restricted_lan

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | H | M | M |
| Product | M | M | M |

Letters are C / H / M / L. Vendor comes from FindUpdates severity, KEV, and exploitability. Product is allowed to be lower when the patched component is not loaded.

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

- `src/HostApplication/HostApplication.csproj` — `OutputType` WinExe, `TargetFramework` `net9.0-windows`, `UseWPF` true; references Core only (no third-party `PackageReference`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `dotnet publish` `-r win-x64` `--self-contained true` `-p:PublishSingleFile=true`; host Win32k/DWM stack is not embedded in the exe.
- `src/HostApplication/MainWindow.xaml` — WPF `Window` with `CenterScreen`, multi-column layout, and theme brushes (host windowing/DPI path).
- `src/HostApplication/app.manifest` — Windows 10 compatibility GUID `{8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a}`, `dpiAware` true/pm, `dpiAwareness` `PerMonitorV2`.
- `src/HostApplication/MainViewModel.cs` — binds UI state; does not load kernel modules; WPF presentation depends on host Win32k.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The exe still starts without this KB. WPF is bundled by self-contained publish; this is a host windowing KB, not a product `PackageReference`.
- **If we install: App may break.** A host Win32k/DWM KB can change DPI or composition used by `MainWindow.xaml` and `app.manifest` (`PerMonitorV2`).
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Leaving the KB off leaves that host windowing stack unpatched. The WPF UI can still launch.
- **Compatibility: Unknown.** We did not prove an API/ABI break against current `main`; windowing/DPI after the KB is not covered by a UI test.

### Conclusions

KB5060001 patches host Win32k/windowing used by the WPF client (`UseWPF`, `MainWindow.xaml`, `app.manifest` `PerMonitorV2`). The product exe remains self-contained on `main`; this KB does not replace WPF bits inside the published zip.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-12345 in KB5060001. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed that the WPF UI module has such host windowing dependency.

## Product Risk assessment

- Affected product functions: WPF windowing, DPI, and composition.
- Potential hazards: operator cannot read the UI if windowing or DPI breaks after the host KB.
- Failure scenarios: install — layout or DPI may break; skip — host windowing stays exposed.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- No Unit, Smoke, or Regression case in `docs/test-plan.md` for this host path.
- No UI automation.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio: lab-check the published win-x64 build for Config1 against this `win32k-wpf` coupling. Do not instruct production install from this analysis.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `dotnet publish` `-r win-x64` `--self-contained true` `-p:PublishSingleFile=true`; host Win32k/DWM stack is not embedded in the exe.
- `src/HostApplication/MainWindow.xaml` — WPF `Window` with `CenterScreen`, multi-column layout, and theme brushes (host windowing/DPI path).
- `src/HostApplication/app.manifest` — Windows 10 compatibility GUID `{8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a}`, `dpiAware` true/pm, `dpiAwareness` `PerMonitorV2`.
- `src/HostApplication/MainViewModel.cs` — binds UI state; does not load kernel modules; WPF presentation depends on host Win32k.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The exe still starts without this KB. WPF is bundled by self-contained publish; this is a host windowing KB, not a product `PackageReference`.
- **If we install: App may break.** A host Win32k/DWM KB can change DPI or composition used by `MainWindow.xaml` and `app.manifest` (`PerMonitorV2`).
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Leaving the KB off leaves that host windowing stack unpatched. The WPF UI can still launch.
- **Compatibility: Unknown.** We did not prove an API/ABI break against current `main`; windowing/DPI after the KB is not covered by a UI test.

### Conclusions

KB5060001 patches host Win32k/windowing used by the WPF client (`UseWPF`, `MainWindow.xaml`, `app.manifest` `PerMonitorV2`). The product exe remains self-contained on `main`; this KB does not replace WPF bits inside the published zip.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-12345 in KB5060001. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed that the WPF UI module has such host windowing dependency.

## Product Risk assessment

- Affected product functions: WPF windowing, DPI, and composition.
- Potential hazards: operator cannot read the UI if windowing or DPI breaks after the host KB.
- Failure scenarios: install — layout or DPI may break; skip — host windowing stays exposed.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- No Unit, Smoke, or Regression case in `docs/test-plan.md` for this host path.
- No UI automation.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio: lab-check the published win-x64 build for Config7 against this `win32k-wpf` coupling. Do not instruct production install from this analysis.

findings.title: Notes stored as plaintext in user AppData
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs writes UTF-8 plaintext via File.WriteAllText to %AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt; MDS2-DATA met (local-only, no PHI, no remote storage). Accepted PoC residual risk is host-account access to the file.

findings.title: No inbound network listener
findings.evidence: No TcpListener, HttpListener, or other bind/listen usage under workspace/HostApplication; sole network use is outbound InsecureVendorBulletinClient.FetchAsync. MDS2-NET met.
